newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish scare stops McDonald burger sales.
newsitem.headline: Danish scare stops McDonald burger sales.

text.p: Fast food chain McDonald's said Friday it suspended sales of hamburgers at its 70 restaurants in Denmark after reports of food poisoning.
"Customers must never be in any doubt about the safety of eating at McDonald's," the chain said in a statement.
"We intend to replace our entire stock this afternoon and evening. In the meantime only soft drinks, deserts and french fries will remain on sale," it said.
McDonalds said all its Danish outlets would resume burger sales on Saturday, using new meat and cheese stocks.
Danish food authorities are investigating 125 reported cases of food poisoning believed to be related to McDonald's Big Mac burgers, the Danish daily Politiken said on Friday.
The symptoms were vomiting, diarrhoea and stomach ache, it said.

McDonalds said the authorities had told them that they had found nothing abnormal in tests on its meat and cheese products and the U.S-based chain criticised officials for not publicising their findings immediately.
